description.narrative: 1. The Supporting Sustainable Economic Recovery Program will help the Cook Islands restore fiscally sustainable growth led by the private sector, which has been adversely affected by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. The program aims to (i) improve fiscal management and sustainability and (ii) strengthen the enabling environment for the private sector. It aligns with Asian Development Bank (ADB) Strategy 2030 operational priorities of strengthening governance and institutional capacity, accelerating progress in gender equality, and fostering regional cooperation and integration. It is consistent with the country operations business plan for Eleven small Pacific island countries, 2021-2023 and Pacific Approach, 2021-2025.

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jan 01, 2022 - Dec 31, 2024

description.narrative:
Action 1: The cabinet approved and MFEM commenced implementation of an updated Medium Term Fiscal Strategy for FY2022-FY2025, which includes cash, debt, and fiscal targets, to provide macroeconomic stability and restore economic growth. Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 2: In order to enable quick action in case of deteriorating economic conditions, thereby supporting continued public sector operations and employment (55.8% women employees):
1.2.1. The cabinet approved the Cash Management Strategy which endorses adjustment measures to be implemented in the event of cash reserves falling below critical limits. 1.2.2. MFEM commenced implementation of the Cash Management Strategy through (i) the operationalization of a new consolidated modeling framework to improve cash management, forecasting and monitoring; and (ii) establishment and operationalization of the monthly Cash Management Committee to strengthen interagency coordination and monitoring and execution of adjustment measures. Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 3: The tax comptroller approved and the Revenue Management Division of MFEM commenced implementation of a compliance improvement strategy for 2020-2022, to improve tax compliance, intensify arrears collections (from those less affected by the pandemic), and accelerate the issuance of refunds.e Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 4: The Parliament passed amendments to the Public Expenditure Review Committee and Audit Act 1995-96 to improve the timeliness and transparency of audit reporting and protect Audit Office staff from prosecution when performing their official duties; and MFEM commenced implementation of the amendments by publishing audited government financial statements and audit reports for FY2015-FY2019 on its website to enhance fiscal transparency. Target date: 2024-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 2 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jan 01, 2022 - Dec 31, 2024

description.narrative:
Policy 2: Reform Area 2: Enabling environment for the private sector. NA
Action 2: The Principal Immigration Officer approved, promulgated with immediate effect, and commenced implementation of revised procedures for the management of migrant worker permits, allowing for greater labor market mobility for migrant workers (to seek employment beyond initial visa sponsors), including a mediation process for the resolution of disputes, to reduce labor market frictions and labor shortages during the economic recovery, which will benefit migrant workers (around half of whom are women). Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 3: The cabinet tabled a new Immigration Bill in Parliament for enactment to improve the transparency and certainty around visa categories and processes, codify migrant worker protections and an appeals process, and enshrine protections for the rights of children, to reduce longer term labor market shortages by improving immigration management, benefiting migrant workers (around half of whom are women). Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 4: In order to reduce business compliance costs and support the use of movable capital in lending:
1.4.1. The cabinet approved, with immediate effect, the Companies Act Regulations 2019, Incorporated Societies Amendment Act Regulations 2019, and the Property Personal Securities Act Regulations 2019 to implement the relevant Acts and allow for the establishment of an online integrated platform for business and securities registration. 1.4.2. The Ministry of Justice implemented the regulations by establishing and operationalizing the online integrated platform which (i) allows for the filing of (and access to) company records, business names, business licenses, and incorporated associations to reduce compliance costs for businesses, and improved access by entrepreneurs (including women) to registry services without the use of lawyers or other proxies; (ii) includes a centralized registry of security interests over movable assets to improve the transparency and reduce the lending risks to the providers of lending instruments; and (iii) enables the collection of sex-disaggregated data on the ownership of companies, committee members of incorporated societies, and over movables assets. Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 5: In order to establish an independent authority to oversee the regulation of the telecommunications sector and reforms, and enable future market-based reforms:
1.5.1. The Parliament passed the Competition and Regulatory Authority Act 2019 to enable the creation of an independent regulator that reports directly to the Parliament. 1.5.2. The government commenced implementation of the Act, by operationalizing the independent Competition and Regulatory Authority through the approval of separate appropriations and the appointment of a chair in order to assure the independence of the authority to perform its role. Target date: 2024-12-31
Action 6: In order to establish regulated competition in the telecommunications sector to allow for improved service delivery and investment opportunities:
1.6.1. The Parliament passed the Telecommunications Act 2019 to enable new market entrants and the regulate wholesale pricing. 1.6.2. The Competition and Regulatory Authority issued telecommunications licenses to new providers under the Act to increase competition in the sector. Target date: 2024-12-31

The Border Easement Taskforce implemented a comprehensive set of initiatives to support the Cook Islands' readiness to receive visitors and to ensure that the quarantine-free travel arrangement with New Zealand is achieved, maintained, and any disruptions addressed. Target date: 2024-12-31
